Anya: heads up — longcontext soak on rtx-pool shows KV cache RSS creeping ~6%/hr. heap snapshots show a huge number of tiny free fragments (mostly 128B-1KB). feels like microhole accumulation rather than outright leak :thinking:

Matt: can you paste the sampling/profile? interested if alloc/free hotspots or just fragmentation metadata growth

Anya: pasted quick notes from the run: free_segments: 1.2M, avg_free_size: 512, free_dist: {128: 420k, 256: 300k, 512: 220k, 1k: 120k}. alloc_path shows a lot of small reclaims and partial fills. perf shows time in slab_alloc_fastpath and split_coalesce.

Liam: that distribution screams slab-size mismatch. maybe our base bucket (4KB) is too coarse and allocator splits into many microblocks, but we never coalesce efficiently.

Sophia: we changed the split threshold in Q4 for latency reasons — lowered coalesce aggressiveness to avoid pauses. that probably reduced compaction. tradeoff bite back in longcontexts.

Tariq: I ran a short A/B this morning: enabling background micro-compactor (nonblocking, rate-limited) reduced microhole count by ~32% over 6h. no noticeable p50 change, p99 increased ~3%.

Anya: interesting. I also profiled kernel selection/batching effects: higher sequence lengths increased reuse of KV entries but also stretched KV lifetime so fragmentation compounds over time. put differently, long contexts keep many small entries alive and cause fragmentation when they get partially freed.

Matt: do we have a cheap heuristic to avoid creating tiny free fragments? e.g., round-up small allocations to 1K or use slab pooling for small entries?

Sophia: we could tune block size buckets: bump smallest bucket to 1KB (was 512), and add a sticky-reuse window so recently-freed small blocks get preferred for small allocs. both are low-risk and implementable in the allocator shim.

Liam: another angle — opportunistic on-alloc coalesce: when allocating, attempt to merge adjacent free microblocks within same slab up to a small budget. cheap and incremental, avoids background task complexity in some cases.

Tariq: caveat: opportunistic coalesce on hot allocation path can increase p50. need strict CPU budget / iteration cap. my micro-test shows cap=8 merges/alloc keeps p50 neutral and halves microholes in that slab.

Anya: posted short flame snippet:

```
# perf top sample
  slab_alloc_fastpath  32%
  split_coalesce       18%
  kv_cache_lookup      12%
  kv_eviction          6%
```

Anya: also pasting a trimmed allocator dump:

```
slab 0x7f8a: total=64MB used=52MB free=12MB fragments=420k avg_frag=384
slab 0x7f9b: total=64MB used=58MB free=6MB fragments=160k avg_frag=512
```

Matt: thanks. seems like compaction improves memory but has latency tradeoffs. we should try two canaries:
1) bucket-tune: raise min-bucket to 1KB + sticky-reuse TTL=30s (no allocator path merges).
2) async-microcompactor: enable background rate-limited coalescer at low priority + keep current bucket config.

Sophia: agree. add a third fast experiment: opportunistic coalesce with strict cap=4 merges/alloc and opportunistic budget only when CPU util < 60%.

Tariq: ran a short canary for (1) yesterday on a single node: fragmentation down 28%, steady-state RSS down 7%, no change in p99 under low load but under realistic qps p99 jitter rose ~2-4%.

Anya: ok let's schedule two 48h canaries across different load shapes: one read-heavy (batching stress), one long-seq heavy. dev-bot can spawn infra.

dev-bot: @channel canary groups created: rv-canary-17 (bucket-tune) + rv-canary-18 (async-microcompactor). nodes: rtx-4a-{11..14}. TTL=48h. logs to /canary/4332109999/

Liam: also add perf counters for split_coalesce and coalesce_attempts to telemetry. want to see per-slab coalesce_efficiency metric.

Anya: adding perf counters + adding sample flamegraph upload to the canary job.

ops-bot: scheduled: runbook bump: if RSS drops <5% after 24h move canary->expanded, if p99 > +10% rollback. Notifying oncall.

Sophia: follow-up: compaction proposal doc draft incoming. will include thresholds, CPU budget params, and benchmark recipes (soaks + p99/throughput). will link here when ready :eyes:

Tariq: one more thought — eviction policy interacts: if we shift to larger buckets we also change eviction granularity. need to validate tail-cost of evicting larger chunks vs more frequent small evictions. add evict-cost sim to the benchmark.

Anya: noted. ok team — action items: (Anya) collect baseline flamegraphs and microhole histogram, (Liam) add telemetry for coalesce counters, (Sophia) draft compaction RFC, (Tariq) run opportunistic coalesce perf microbench, (Matt) coordinate canary rollout and monitoring.
